beforeGuidance: Requires Strength, Dexterity, Constitution 15 and Intelligence, Wisdom 10; confirm service, social station, sponsorship, and any zero-level stages.
At each higher level, increase the Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution percentiles by the specified 2d10 procedure.
Below the self-training threshold, train with a cavalier of at least level 4 or two levels higher, whichever is greater.
After reaching level 6, the normal regimen suffices for training; mount and weapon abilities continue to change.
appendedGuidance: UA p. 13 Table II lists the cavalier for any armor, shield, and weapons, subject to note 1’s social-station limits on armor and arms; note 2 bars oil in personal combat but permits siege use, and poison is listed only if evil. Use the six social-station packages on p. 25; each horse is supplied with station-appropriate tack, harness, saddle, and saddlebags, and a cavalier below Upper Class begins as a 0-level Horseman to be taken in by a good family and esquired.

UA p. 26 lists the cavalier weapon-proficiency row as 3*, a −3 nonproficiency penalty, and one added proficiency per two levels. Its star note specifies 0-level Horseman/Lancer and 1st-level Armiger counts and restricts Cavalier weapon choices.

beforeGuidance: Meet cavalier requirements plus Wisdom 13 and Charisma 17; remain lawful good.
Correct social station or noble sponsorship is required; sponsorship can require both zero-level stages.
UA removes the prime requisite and its exceptional-ability XP bonus.
Apply cavalier weapon, parry, horsemanship, fear, saving-throw, and ability-improvement features, including Charisma improvement.

Source conflict in the ordinary thrusting/striking weapon attack table: UA p.22 puts level 12 in both 7–12 at 3 attacks/2 rounds and 12–18 at 2/round. The stated under-one-HD/normal-human melee case and fighter/ranger specialization use separate rules. PHB p.25 instead begins 2/round at 13th. Preserve the internal UA overlap without choosing a universal level-12 rate.
appendedGuidance: UA p. 13 Table II lists any armor, shield, and weapons subject to note 1’s social-station limits; note 2 bars oil in personal combat but permits siege use, and poison is never permitted.

UA p. 26 shows a starred Paladin weapon-proficiency entry (3*, −3, one added proficiency per two levels). The star note defines zero-level Cavalier grades and names Cavalier/Ranger weapon-choice restrictions, but does not explain the Paladin star; keep that meaning unresolved.

beforeGuidance: The Grand Druid is level 15, with at least 3,000,001 XP; the office carries special responsibilities and benefits.
After at least 3,500,001 XP, a Grand Druid may seek a successor and abdicate.
On entering the level-16 Hierophant path, the XP total resets to 1 and office-related bonus spells are relinquished.
Use the separate Hierophant table and planar abilities; do not extrapolate the PHB druid table.
appendedGuidance: UA p. 13 Table II restricts the Druid to leather or padded armor, a wooden shield, and the listed weapons (aklys, club, dagger, dart, garrot, hammer, lasso, sap, sling, scimitar, spear, staff, staff sling, sword (khopesh), and whip); oil is permitted and poison is the DM’s option.
UA p. 26 lists the Druid weapon-proficiency row as 2 initial weapons, a −4 nonproficiency penalty, and one added proficiency per five levels.

beforeGuidance: Human and non-lawful: Strength 15, Dexterity 14, Constitution 15; Wisdom may not exceed 16.
No prime requisite grants bonus XP, and a player barbarian cannot be a two-class character.
Update class skills and the level-based ability to harm creatures otherwise requiring magical weapons.
After level 8, gain 4 hp per level instead of another hit die; check changing restrictions on magic use.
appendedGuidance: UA p. 13 Table II permits any armor, shield, and weapons, but note 3 limits the class Dexterity armor benefit in bulky or fairly bulky armor.

UA p. 18 requires the barbarian’s initial weapon proficiencies to include hand axe, knife, and spear; other weapons based on the native area may be chosen by the DM. The p. 26 weapon table lists six initial proficiencies, a −1 nonproficiency penalty, and one added proficiency per two levels; these weapon slots are separate from the barbarian’s nonweapon abilities.

UA pp. 19–20 group barbarian abilities as eight primary abilities (climbing, hiding, surprise, back protection, leaping/springing, detecting illusion, detecting magic, leadership), four secondary abilities (survival, first aid, outdoor craft, tracking), and one or more locale- or culture-selected tertiary skills. All four secondary abilities are possessed, but are generally limited in unfamiliar areas until about a month of continuous exposure; the DM determines applicable tertiary skills. Paddled and rowed small craft are separate tertiary options.

beforeGuidance: Requires Strength 15 and Dexterity 16, and five completed thief levels.
On qualifying for level 6, train for six weeks under a thief-acrobat of at least level 10.
Pick pockets, opening locks, and finding/removing traps stop improving at their level-5 ability; magical writing is never gained.

Use the specialist acrobatics tables and explicit climbing progression. UA pp.23 and 25 describe stopped, retained and generally inherited thief abilities; later progression of the four retained skills remains a campaign interpretation.
appendedGuidance: UA p. 13 Table II lists the Acrobat’s armor as “as thief,” no shield, and weapons “as thief, plus lasso and staff”; oil is permitted and poison is the DM’s option. Note 4 directs armor other than leather to the function adjustments in Thieves Table II (p. 22).

UA p. 25 Tables II and III adjust the Acrobat’s base function chances or maxima for Strength and Dexterity; apply their stated racial adjustments as well. Table IV separates body-associated weight (clothing, accessories, armor, weapons) from additional carried weight, which applies only while tightrope walking; backpacks are otherwise barred during Acrobat activities. Its level-14 extra 1,000 gp and level-22 passenger examples are limited by the accompanying procedure.
UA p. 26 lists the Acrobat weapon-proficiency row as 2 initial weapons, a −3 nonproficiency penalty, and one added proficiency per four levels.

beforeGuidance: Requires Strength 9 and Constitution 7.
Check the attacks-per-round table when reaching a new combat band.
After level 9, gain 3 hp per level instead of another hit die.
At level 9, establishing and clearing a freehold can attract men-at-arms and revenue.
appendedGuidance: UA p. 13 Table II lists the Fighter for any armor, shield, and weapons; oil is permitted and poison is the DM’s option. UA p. 26 lists four initial weapon proficiencies, a −2 nonproficiency penalty, and one added proficiency per three levels.

UA p. 18 allows weapon specialization only for Fighters and Rangers, chosen at character creation and costing two weapon-proficiency slots. From the initial allotment of four Fighter or three Ranger weapons, ordinary specialization leaves one specialist weapon plus two or one other proficient weapons; bow specialization (but not crossbow specialization) costs one extra slot, leaving the Fighter one other proficiency and the Ranger none. A melee specialist gains +1 to hit and +2 damage. A bow specialist has 6–30-foot point-blank range (+2 to hit and damage, double damage on a successful hit) and +1 to hit and damage at short range; the bow can be fired before initiative if the arrow is nocked, shaft drawn, and target in sight. A crossbow specialist has 6–60-foot point-blank range (+2 to hit and damage, double damage), short range +1 to hit and damage, and medium range +1 to hit only; it can fire before initiative if cocked, aimed, and the target is in range. Other missile specialists gain +1 to hit and +2 damage. Specialization hit bonuses are not magical and do not enable hits on creatures affected only by magical weapons. Use the existing UA specialization-rate table for weapon-specific rates; it supersedes ordinary rates while the specialist weapon is used.

beforeGuidance: Requires Strength 13, Intelligence 13, Wisdom 14, and Constitution 14; alignment must remain good.
The first level starts with two hit dice, rather than one.
Druidic spells begin at level 8, and magic-user spells at level 9.
At level 10, check followers and new item use; after level 10, gain 2 hp per level.
appendedGuidance: UA p. 13 Table II lists the Ranger for any armor, shield, and weapons; oil is permitted and poison is the DM’s option. UA p. 26 lists three initial weapon proficiencies*, a −2 nonproficiency penalty, and one added proficiency per three levels; the star note restricts Ranger weapon choices.

UA p. 18 allows weapon specialization only for Fighters and Rangers, chosen at character creation and costing two weapon-proficiency slots. From the initial allotment of four Fighter or three Ranger weapons, ordinary specialization leaves one specialist weapon plus two or one other proficient weapons; bow specialization (but not crossbow specialization) costs one extra slot, leaving the Fighter one other proficiency and the Ranger none. A melee specialist gains +1 to hit and +2 damage. A bow specialist has 6–30-foot point-blank range (+2 to hit and damage, double damage on a successful hit) and +1 to hit and damage at short range; the bow can be fired before initiative if the arrow is nocked, shaft drawn, and target in sight. A crossbow specialist has 6–60-foot point-blank range (+2 to hit and damage, double damage), short range +1 to hit and damage, and medium range +1 to hit only; it can fire before initiative if cocked, aimed, and the target is in range. Other missile specialists gain +1 to hit and +2 damage. Specialization hit bonuses are not magical and do not enable hits on creatures affected only by magical weapons. Use the existing UA specialization-rate table for weapon-specific rates; it supersedes ordinary rates while the specialist weapon is used.

UA pp. 21–22 add situation-specific tracking procedures to the Ranger’s level-by-level base chances already recorded in this class entry. Outdoors, the base is 10% per level plus 10%, with a 110% base ceiling; terrain, group size, crossing/overtracking, trail age, precipitation, and deliberate concealment modify the attempt. Indoor tracking uses separate surface categories, the same base and specified shared modifiers, and additional observation prerequisites; movement rate depends on track clarity and illumination. Apply the printed definitions and impossibility limits, and keep the p. 22 identification roll separate from the tracking roll.

notes.summary: Cavalier/Paladin armor and weapon permissions are constrained by social station; note 1 excludes lower-class armor and pole arms, missile weapons, and other arms associated with lower social classes.
Cavalier/Paladin may not use oil in personal combat but may use it in siege warfare.
Barbarian may use any armor but does not receive the full class Dexterity benefit in bulky or fairly bulky armor.
A thief in armor other than leather takes specified adjustments to thief-function chances; see Thieves Table II.
A class-unpermitted weapon can be picked up and used at the most severe applicable nonproficiency penalty, but cannot be kept or carried for later use.

A character under five feet cannot effectively use a long bow or a weapon over twelve feet. Under 100 pounds cannot use a heavy crossbow, a pole arm weighing over 200 gp, or a two-handed sword; these physical limits override the preceding permission rule.

details.preconditions: Indoor tracking requires the Ranger to have observed a distinguishing feature of the tracks and to have observed the quarry making the trail, then to follow within a reasonable period (typically 10–30 minutes). The source directs the DM to use common sense; unusual visual, audio, olfactory or other evidence can sometimes make a trail possible.
details.chanceLimit: Adjusted outdoor chance over 100% is treated as 100%; negative adjustments may reduce it below 100%.
details.definitions: Obvious: at least 71% chance; occasional: 31–70%; faint: 30% or less. Poor illumination is less than daylight but more than total darkness; total darkness prevents tracking unless nonvisual evidence is available.
details.identification: The p. 22 ten-level identification table, separate second roll, and cumulative abilities are already represented in ranger.levelChanges; intentionally no duplicate is proposed.
